note: Floor for regression against testing/eval/eval_gold.jsonl (1455 rows, independently hand-labeled per testing/eval/RUBRIC.md, not derived from filters.py). Eval uses classify_job_fields(us_only=False, drop_interns=False, swe_only=False) so it measures raw classifier quality, not scope filtering (matches tests/test_eval_regression.py). Precision is well-measured: the gold set includes essentially every regex-positive job found while sampling ~44,600 live postings across 128 companies (three fetch rounds, the last uncapped/full). Recall is better-measured than in earlier rounds but still not representative of true production recall - the sample remains stratified toward regex-positive and known-hard-exclude categories, not a random draw of the huge 'obvious reject' population. History: round 1 (226 rows) P=0.5273->0.8056. Round 2 expanded to 484 rows, re-exposing gaps: P=0.6250->0.7143. Round 3 (2026-08-26) added 971 more rows (fetched uncapped across all 128 companies, ~38k postings sampled) for much stronger statistical confidence, taking the set to 1455 rows; the larger sample again re-exposed real gaps (P=0.6574/R=0.9098 before fixes) which a fourth fix pass addressed: (1) 'mentor(ing) junior/other engineers' added as a general senior-experience signal (directionally safe - does not match 'mentored by' / 'paired with a mentor' receiving-side phrasing) - this alone fixed ~19 cases and retroactively resolved an unfixed case from round 1 (Glean); (2) broadened non-technical title coverage for data-center/colocation electrical-mechanical facilities engineering (order-independent matching), career-returner/returnship programs, consulting-track internships, bare 'Network Infrastructure Engineer' (technician-level cabling/build work at cloud providers), business-developer titles, and brand/graphic designer roles; (3) added 'Analyst II/III' to the numbered-ladder experienced-title pattern (alongside the existing Engineer/Scientist II-IV coverage); (4) added the 'Snr.' abbreviation alongside 'Sr.' to the senior-keyword patterns. All fixes verified against the full 561-title production corpus after every change, with at most 1-7 titles changing per fix (all confirmed correct, zero unintended regressions). Precision moved 0.6574->0.74, recall unchanged relative to the pre-fix measurement on this set (0.9098; the 35 FN are unaffected by these fixes) after the pass. Explicitly NOT fixed in this round, despite clear evidence: (a) effective_strong_ec() lets a bare EC-sounding phrase (e.g. 'recent graduate', 'pursuing a Master's degree' in a PREFERRED-qualifications aside) override an already-detected real senior-years bar (has_senior_exp=True) - now evidenced by 8+ cases (Broadcom + a 7-posting Anduril 'Manufacturing Test/Software Engineer' cluster all requiring stated 4-5+ years) but left alone because this function is used broadly enough elsewhere that a targeted change carries real risk of side effects; flagged as the single highest-value candidate for a dedicated, carefully-tested follow-up pass. (b) The SpaceX mechanical/electrical/aerospace-adjacent title boundary (~39 remaining FP + all 35 FN) - a large, genuinely disputed zone (hands-on design/build/test vs. process/manufacturing/facilities) that this project's own labeling has never fully reconciled even across three independent hand-labeling rounds; documented, not patched, since resolving it either way in the regex would be company-specific overfitting. Prior superseded baselines: P=0.6636/R=0.7933 (2026-06-27, unverifiable non-existent corpus); round-1's 0.5273/0.8056; round-2's 0.6250/0.7143 (both on smaller gold sets, superseded by this round's much larger sample).
